correctness.rationale: Wuebben's Theorem 5.6 supplies the unique \(\mathbb F_1\)-cone germ and the smooth crepant resolution with Hodge numbers \((4,108)\). The link is the unit circle bundle of \(K_{\mathbb F_1}\). With \(K_{\mathbb F_1}=-2S-3F\), its Euler class evaluates as \((-1,-2)\) on \((S,F)\), so the circle bundle is simply connected and the integral Gysin sequence gives \(H^2\cong H^3\cong\mathbf Z\) with no torsion. The pulled-back second Stiefel--Whitney class vanishes because \(w_2(\mathbb F_1)\equiv c_1(\mathbb F_1)\equiv -K_{\mathbb F_1}\pmod2\), whose pullback is zero. Smale--Barden therefore identifies the link as \(S^2\times S^3\). Additivity gives \(-208-4+1=-211\). Odd Euler characteristic rules out rational Poincaré duality in dimension \(6\).

value.rationale: Wuebben's \(X_C\) is a minimal compact example with exactly one reduced-rigid nonsmoothable singularity. Identifying its link as \(S^2\times S^3\) gives a complete and recognizable local topological type, while the odd ordinary Euler characteristic \(-211\) provides a global topological obstruction stronger in kind than the deformation-theoretic nonsmoothability statement: the underlying space is not even a rational Poincaré-duality \(6\)-space. These are natural structural invariants of the distinguished one-point example.
